I don't understand this section:
`window_fullsize` is set to `window_fullsize_cache`, which is always `0`, since it is never changed.
As a result, `window_fullsize = get_window()->get_size().x;` is always executed.

Sa explained [above](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/pull/122095/changes#r3715790913), `window_size_cache` and `window_fullsize` are both always `get_window()->get_size().x`, so `difference` is `0`.

`&variable_name` is a reference to the variable it is set as, so when `window_fullsize` is changed the underlying `window_fullsize_cache` is also changed. You can see the same thing with `title_size_cache`. It is set as a reference to the specific element in the `title_size_chach` HashMap
There is a difference. Refer to this [comment](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/pull/122095#discussion_r3715826376)
Ah, yes. I looked over that.

Here you set `tag_size_cache` to `MIN(tag_size, tag_maxsize)`:
That means `tag_size_cache` will never be greater than the max. size of **one** tag.
I don't understand this line. Why not use `tag_size`?

if `!autowrap` the function will continue down to the next if statement, which is by design, that function is only intended to remove the autowrap from the `project_title` if was previously autowrapped and now has enough space that the autowrap is no longer needed.

I had to change this because I redesigned the code above it to be stepped over, instead of consantly being called. Because that code is now stepped over, this has to be able to be stepped over as well.

the maximum size of all tags is `336 * EDSCALE`, so regardless of how long a tag's name is, it will never get longer than that value. I only want the title to give allowance for one such tag, either many smaller ones that make up the value or one really big one that takes up all of the space itself.
Yeah I changed it back

### 6. This is solved differently in https://github.com/godotengine/godot/pull/122061
- Probably the solution there is easier to understand.
Yes, https://github.com/godotengine/godot/pull/122061 returns early, if no changes needed.
But why step over if it is easier and probably faster to return early?
Stepping over it is faster because less code gets executed. Also, there is no point in executing that code every time

I compared the two variants:

### Variant 1 (suggested)

- First checks only `p_title_size >= title_fullsize_cache + tag_fullsize_cache`. 
- Calls `get_autowrap_mode()` only if the size is large enough. 
- No additional boolean cache, no redundant boundary check. 
- Fewer conditions, less work in the "wrap" case. 
-> Faster

### Variant 2

- Always calls `project_title->get_autowrap_mode()`, even if the size is too small anyway. 
- Has two compound conditions:
- 1. `autowrap && p_title_size > title_fullsize_cache + tag_size_cache`
- 2. `p_title_size < title_fullsize_cache + tag_size_cache`
- More comparisons, more logical operations.
-> Slower

So, Variant 1 (suggested variant) should be the better solution.
